rationale: The cassette totals 5,340 bp: AAV2 ITRs, the 1,639 bp CAG promoter, a 3,186 bp payload and the 225 bp bGH polyA. That is 640 bp over the 4,700 bp single stranded target and 140 bp over the 5,200 bp hard ceiling, so aav.packaging_limit is the check that must catch it: it is the only check that measures 5' ITR start through 3' ITR end against the band, and above the soft limit its severity is FAIL rather than WARN. A capsid cannot package this genome, so the run would produce truncated species. The case also asserts the remediation field, because section 6.5 requires a FAIL here to name a specific element substitution that would fix it, computed from the part registry. The payload is a length-calibrated tandem concatenation of whole in-frame copies of the real beta-lactamase reading frame of pUC19, GenBank L09137.1 (tests/fixtures/parser/puc19.gb) with one terminal stop codon, assembled only to put the cassette at the exact length this case is about. It is not a real gene and nothing here presents it as one; the defect under test is the length, not the payload. Three checks WARN, and all three are declared here because they follow from the payload and the promoter this case needs rather than from the packaging defect. aav.internal_repeats reports 4 direct repeats over 20 bp in the 5,050 bp inter-ITR region, the longest 1,467 bp at cassette positions 1,785 and 3,501, which is unavoidable because the payload is a tandem concatenation of copies of one reading frame and a concatenation of copies is a direct repeat by construction. aav.homopolymer_runs reports the 14 base G run at cassette position 558, inside the CAG promoter. aav.kozak_context reports the context GGCAAAATGA as adequate but not optimal, because position +4 is A rather than G, which is a property of the payload's first codon. None of the three is a FAIL and none of them measures length, so aav.packaging_limit remains the only failure. Systemic note recorded rather than engineered around: the real promoter.cag record carries a 14 base G run at its offset 412 and the real promoter.cbh record a 16 base G run at its offset 393, both over the 8 bp reporting threshold, so any design built on either promoter trips aav.homopolymer_runs. That is a property of the registry sequences, not of this case, and a CAG design can therefore never be fully isolated from it. Removing the warning would mean either editing a real part, which section 4.3 forbids, or abandoning CAG, which is the promoter this case is sized around.

4,800 bp: 100 bp over the 4,700 bp target and 100 bp under the 4,900 bp soft limit. The verdict must be WARN and not FAIL, because a genome in that band packages with reduced efficiency rather than not at all, and flattening it to FAIL would reject designs that real laboratories run. aav.packaging_limit is the check under test and this case pins the lower boundary of its band, which is the number most likely to drift. The remediation is asserted here too: section 6.5 requires the overage in base pairs, and the engine supplies the substitutions alongside it. The payload is a length-calibrated tandem concatenation of whole in-frame copies of the real beta-lactamase reading frame of pUC19, GenBank L09137.1 (tests/fixtures/parser/puc19.gb) with one terminal stop codon, assembled only to put the cassette at the exact length this case is about. It is not a real gene and nothing here presents it as one; the defect under test is the length, not the payload. The same three warnings fire here as in the hard limit case above, for the same reasons, and are declared rather than left implicit: aav.internal_repeats on 4 direct repeats in the 4,510 bp inter-ITR region, the longest 927 bp at cassette positions 1,785 and 3,501, which the tandem payload makes unavoidable; aav.homopolymer_runs on the 14 base G run at cassette position 558 inside the CAG promoter; and aav.kozak_context on the context GGCAAAATGA, where position +4 is A rather than G. All three are WARN, as is the packaging verdict this case is about, so the case asserts the severity of the named check and not of the overall report alone. Systemic note recorded rather than engineered around: the real promoter.cag record carries a 14 base G run at its offset 412 and the real promoter.cbh record a 16 base G run at its offset 393, both over the 8 bp reporting threshold, so any design built on either promoter trips aav.homopolymer_runs. That is a property of the registry sequences, not of this case, and a CAG design can therefore never be fully isolated from it. Removing the warning would mean either editing a real part, which section 4.3 forbids, or abandoning CAG, which is the promoter this case is sized around.

A 3,000 bp cassette that is entirely legal as a single stranded genome, 1,700 bp under the 4,700 bp target, but is declared self complementary. A self complementary genome is an inverted repeat of the cassette, so the capsid has to hold roughly twice the length and the usable capacity halves: 3,000 bp is 600 bp over the 2,400 bp self complementary target and 400 bp over the 2,600 bp hard ceiling. aav.sc_capacity is the check that must catch it, and aav.packaging_limit must NOT fail, because the length is fine for the single stranded modality it is not using. That split is the whole point of the case: it proves the halved band is applied to the right designs and that the failure names the reason. The payload is a length-calibrated tandem concatenation of whole in-frame copies of the real beta-lactamase reading frame of pUC19, GenBank L09137.1 (tests/fixtures/parser/puc19.gb) with one terminal stop codon, assembled only to put the cassette at the exact length this case is about. It is not a real gene and nothing here presents it as one; the defect under test is the length, not the payload. Two checks WARN and are declared here. aav.internal_repeats reports 2 direct repeats over 20 bp in the 2,710 bp inter-ITR region, the longest 858 bp at cassette positions 837 and 1,695, which is inherent to a payload built by concatenating copies of one reading frame to hit an exact length. aav.kozak_context reports the context CAAGCTATGA as adequate but not optimal, because position +4 is A rather than G. Neither is a FAIL and neither concerns capacity, so aav.sc_capacity is the only failure and aav.packaging_limit still passes, which is the split the case exists to prove. This design uses promoter.gfap, which carries no long homopolymer, so unlike the two packaging limit cases it does not also trip aav.homopolymer_runs.

The 3' ITR element is absent. The ITRs are the only viral sequence a recombinant AAV genome retains and they are required in cis for replication and packaging, so a cassette with one ITR does not become a vector at all. aav.itr_present_both is the check that must catch it, because it is the only one that asks whether both ITRs exist and match the serotype reference. aav.itr_orientation and aav.itr_internal_sites report UNKNOWN rather than PASS, which is correct: with one ITR there is no pair to orient and no interior between two ITRs to scan. Neither may be read as a pass and neither is a FAIL, so this case still has exactly one failure.

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: Both ITR slots carry the left ITR as written, so the two repeats are in tandem rather than inverted. Each ITR on its own matches the AAV2 reference, so aav.itr_present_both passes and cannot catch this: the defect is purely relative orientation. aav.itr_orientation is the check that must catch it, decided from the 20 nt D element, which in a correct inverted pair faces inward from both ends and here faces the same way twice. A tandem pair does not form the hairpin the replication machinery needs, so the genome does not replicate or package.

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

elements.name: AAV2 left ITR placed as the 3' ITR

rationale: The polyA element is removed entirely. Without a polyadenylation signal the transcript is not cleaved or polyadenylated, so it is unstable and poorly exported and the vector expresses almost nothing. aav.required_elements is the check that must catch it, because promoter, coding sequence and polyA are the three elements it exists to confirm. aav.polya_present_functional also fails, and that is a genuine cascade from the one defect rather than a second defect: check 12 asks whether the polyA present is a recognised functional signal, and with no polyA element at all there is nothing for it to recognise, which section 6.4 says is a FAIL and not an UNKNOWN. Both failures name the same missing element, so it is listed in allowed_extra_fail rather than hidden, and the two of them are the only non-pass checks in the report. The payload is sized deliberately and the reason is worth recording. With the 405 bp reading frame the companion cases use, removing the 225 bp polyA left a 1,975 bp cassette, 25 bp under the 2,000 bp minimum, so aav.minimum_genome_size warned as well and the case quietly exercised a size floor it is not about. The payload here is that same real reading frame with a declared 60 bp in-frame block of real sequence inserted before its stop codon, which puts the cassette at 2,035 bp, 35 bp clear of the floor. That removes the unrelated warning without touching the defect, the verdict or the named check. The companion case to aav.bad.missing_promoter, with the other required element; that case keeps its size warning because a 691 bp promoter cannot be compensated for the same way.

elements.name: orf465_bla_segment_with_in_frame_filler
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand, with a 60 bp in-frame block inserted immediately before the natural stop codon. The inserted 60 bp is the plus strand slice of GenBank AF396260.1, CMV promoter (part promoter.cmv) at offset 53, which carries no stop codon in this frame. The insertion is deliberate and declared: it is length filler, chosen only to put the cassette over the 2,000 bp minimum genome size, and it is not presented as coding for anything

rationale: A 135 bp real fragment of pUC19 occupies the polyA slot. It is the right size for a polyA and it is real DNA, so every structural check passes and aav.required_elements is satisfied by the element being present, but it carries neither AATAAA nor ATTAAA, so it is not a polyadenylation signal. This is the mistake of annotating the wrong fragment as the polyA, which no length or order check can see. aav.polya_present_functional is the only check that reads the sequence for a recognised hexamer, and section 6.4 gives it WARN for an unrecognised signal rather than FAIL, because a functional signal this module does not know is possible and the user is better placed to judge.

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

elements.name: mis-annotated 135 bp fragment
elements.source: pUC19, GenBank L09137.1 (tests/fixtures/parser/puc19.gb) plus strand 1..135, placed in the polyA slot

rationale: Codon 21 of the real reading frame is replaced by TAA, giving a premature in-frame stop while the length, the start codon and the terminal stop all stay correct. The vector would be built, would package and would express a 20 residue fragment instead of the protein, which is the expensive kind of mistake because nothing about the construct looks wrong. aav.cds_integrity is the only check that translates the reading frame, so it is the only one that can catch this, and its message gives the cassette position of the offending codon. The substitution is synthetic and deliberate: the point is the defect, and everything around it is the real frame.

elements.name: orf405 with a premature stop at codon 21
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: One base is removed from the 3' end of the real reading frame, so the coding sequence is 404 bp. The length is not divisible by three, which means the reading frame does not close and the terminal stop codon is no longer in frame. This is the classic one base cloning slip. aav.cds_integrity is the check that must catch it, and it reports both consequences and says how many bases to add or remove. It is a separate case from the premature stop because a single check with several conditions can pass one and fail another, and both conditions are named in section 6.4 check 6.

elements.name: orf405 with one 3' base removed
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: Every required element is present and every sequence is real, but the polyA sits between the promoter and the coding sequence instead of after it. Transcription would terminate and polyadenylate before reaching the transgene, so the cassette expresses nothing. aav.required_elements passes, because presence is all it checks, and the length is unchanged, so aav.element_order is the only check that can catch this: it compares the element roles against the section 6.2 functional order. The Kozak warning that comes with it is a true consequence of the polyA now sitting in front of the start codon, and it is a WARN, so the case still has exactly one failure.

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: A liver-targeted vector driven by the hSyn1 promoter, which is neuron specific. The cassette is 2,437 bp, structurally perfect and comfortably inside the packaging band, so no length or structural check sees anything: this is precisely the design error section 6.2 says no length check will catch. The transgene would simply not be expressed in hepatocytes. aav.promoter_tissue_match is the check that must catch it, comparing the part's tissue_specificity annotation with the requested target_tissue, and the severity is WARN because the designer, not the registry, knows the intended cell type. The payload is the complete 861 bp beta-lactamase reading frame of pUC19, GenBank L09137.1 (tests/fixtures/parser/puc19.gb), ATG through TAA, whose native initiation context also warns; that is a WARN, so the case still reports no failure at all, which is the expected outcome.

A 60 bp stretch of the reading frame is duplicated in frame immediately after itself, so the cassette carries a 60 bp direct repeat between the ITRs while the coding sequence stays a clean open reading frame: the duplication is a whole number of codons and adds no stop, so aav.cds_integrity still passes and cannot catch it. Direct repeats above 20 bp recombine during vector production, which deletes the intervening sequence and yields a mixed, partly truncated preparation. aav.internal_repeats is the only check that looks for repeated substrings inside the cassette, so it is the one that must catch it. The duplication is a deliberate synthetic edit to a real frame.

elements.name: orf405 with a 60 bp in-frame duplication
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: An 887 bp cassette: AAV2 ITRs, the 225 bp MeCP2 mini promoter, a 237 bp payload and the 135 bp SV40 polyA, with no WPRE. Everything is structurally correct, the promoter matches the cns_neuron target and the reading frame is clean, so the only thing wrong is that the genome is 1,113 bp below the 2,000 bp floor. Genomes this small package inefficiently and raise the empty capsid fraction, so the titer per production run drops. aav.minimum_genome_size is the only check that looks at the lower end of the band, which makes it the one that must catch it, and it is a WARN because the vector does work, just less well, and the fix is to add stuffer sequence.

elements.name: orf237_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: Both ITRs are present and in the inverted orientation, but the 5' ITR carries 21 transversions, one every seventh base, dropping its identity to the AAV2 reference to 85.5%, below the 0.95 threshold. aav.itr_present_both is the check that must catch it, because it is the one that measures identity against the serotype reference rather than merely counting elements, and that distinction is what makes presence checking useful. It is the only failure in the report. aav.itr_orientation still decides inverted and passes, but not because the D element was left alone: three of the 21 substitutions, at positions 127, 134 and 141, fall inside the terminal 20 nt D element, which takes that window to 85.0% identity, under the 95% anchor threshold, so the D element cannot be located in the 5' ITR at all. Orientation therefore falls through to its documented second method, the identity margin: the 5' ITR matches the reverse complement of the 3' ITR at 75.0% against 66.1% for the tandem arrangement, a separation of 8.9% that clears the 5% margin, so inverted is called on evidence and not by default. That is what isolates the defect, and it is a stronger result than an untouched anchor would be: this is an ITR that is in the right place and demonstrably the right way round under a method that does not depend on the bases that were changed, and is simply no longer an AAV2 ITR. It is also the only case in the set that reaches the orientation fallback path, so it is the only one that shows the fallback works.

elements.name: degenerate 5' ITR
elements.source: AAV2 left ITR (itr.aav2_itr_left) with 21 transversions introduced for this case, one every seventh base, three of them at positions 127, 134 and 141 inside the terminal 20 nt D element

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: The promoter element is removed, so the coding sequence sits directly against the 5' ITR. Nothing drives transcription, so the vector packages and expresses nothing. aav.required_elements is the check that must catch it, and it is the only failure in the report. One other check correctly declines to guess: aav.promoter_tissue_match reports UNKNOWN because there is no promoter annotation to compare with the target tissue, which must never read as a pass. It is listed in expected_unknown, and it is the only UNKNOWN. Two checks WARN, and both follow from removing the promoter rather than from a second defect, so they are declared here. aav.kozak_context warns because the initiator ATG now sits against the ITR instead of a promoter, giving the context GTTCCTATGG, whose position -3 is C where a purine is required; that warning is the direct consequence of the deletion and cannot be removed while the promoter is missing. aav.minimum_genome_size warns because the removed promoter is 691 bp, leaving a 1,509 bp cassette, 491 bp under the 2,000 bp floor; it cannot be engineered away either, because the largest real payload available here is the full 861 bp beta-lactamase reading frame and substituting it would still leave 1,965 bp, under the floor. That is the difference from the companion case aav.bad.no_polya, where the missing element is only 225 bp and the payload can be enlarged to clear the floor, which is why that case has no incidental warnings and this one has two. The companion case to aav.bad.no_polya, with the other required element.

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: Twelve adenines are inserted in frame into the reading frame, which is four lysine codons, so the open reading frame stays clean and aav.cds_integrity passes. A run of twelve identical bases is over the 8 bp threshold: long homopolymers cause polymerase slippage during synthesis and during vector replication, so the ordered DNA and the packaged genome can both differ from the design. aav.homopolymer_runs is the only check that measures single base runs, so it is the one that must catch it. The insertion is a deliberate synthetic edit to a real frame, chosen to be in frame precisely so that no other check can fire.

elements.name: orf405 with a 12 base adenine run inserted in frame
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: The first 21 bases of the AAV2 ITR are inserted in frame into the payload, so ITR sequence sits inside the cassette as well as at both ends. The ITRs themselves are correct and correctly oriented, and the reading frame survives because the insertion is a whole number of codons that adds no stop. An internal ITR motif gives the replication machinery a third place to resolve, which produces snapback and truncated genomes during production. aav.itr_internal_sites is the check that exists for exactly this and it is the only one that compares the interior against the serotype ITR reference on both strands. It is the only non-pass check in the report. The check reports 6 internal 20 bp motifs and all 6 come from the single insertion, which is worth saying because 6 hits could otherwise read as 6 defects. The 21 inserted bases, together with the G that already preceded them in the payload, give 22 contiguous bases that match the AAV2 reference pair, so exactly three overlapping 20 bp windows fit inside that stretch; the check counts each of those three windows once on the plus strand and once as its reverse complement on the minus strand, because an internal terminal repeat is a substrate for aberrant resolution on either strand. Three windows on two strands is 6 hits of one defect. The insertion is a deliberate synthetic edit and is declared as one; the 21 bases themselves are the real first 21 bases of itr.aav2_itr_left and the payload around them is the real reading frame, unedited.

elements.name: orf405 with a 21 bp ITR motif inserted in frame
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand
